newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks finish firmer as futures fly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks finish firmer as futures fly.

text.p: SPI futures 2435 +17 US 30yr cl 6.87 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.170 +0.075 Gold NY 358.75 Lon fix 361.75
*Stocks end just firmer, futures-linked buying lifts market off floor in afternoon session. Vol 321.08 million, value A$648.56 million, 1,115 stocks traded, 324 steady, 325 up, 466 down.
Australian shares closed just firmer on Wednesday with futures-linked buying in the afternoon lifting the market back to better than square for the day.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 0.9 points higher at 2,433.0.
The March share price index futures contract was up 17 points at 2,435, a two point premium to the index.

While the market dipped early on nervousness ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, due later today, brokers said strong demand for the leaders emerged late in the day as futures flew home.
"There has been hectic trade in the SPI and that has pulled the leaders out of the hole," said a Sydney broker.
"BHP, CRA and the banks all had big comebacks. That discount has narrowed quite a bit since Monday so I think you have seen some arbitrage play going on."
Other traders agreed, saying there appeared to be a lack of real reasons for the change in sentiment late in the day.

"Somebody is trading between the markets with some quite good volumes," said broker Grant Williams of Reynolds and Co, although he noted that the early weakness had been more than most expected in any case.
December quarter GDP figures were largely in line with expectations and failed to have much impact.
Oil and gas major Woodside Petroleum jumped 31.7 cents to close at its day's high of A$8.977 after its 58 percent higher full year net profit of A$190.96 million.

Building materials group, Boral, added six cents to A$3.50 after its first half net profit of A$93.16 million, while fellow building materials group, Pioneer International, was active with 7.7 million shares traded, the bulk in three lines totalling six million though Merrill Lynch. Pioneer shares closed six cents higher at A$3.97.
GIO Australia featured in turnover lists early with volume topping 5.1 million shares after the insurance group went ex-dividend 10 cents.
Coal producer QCT Resources ended steady at A$1.75 after its marginally lower first half net profit of A$30.29 million.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting ended a cent higher at A$6.35 after a slightly lower first half net profit of A$104.3 million, while homeware products supplier McPherson's lost five cents to A$3.90 despite a sharply higher first half net profit.
Financial services group Tyndall Australia closed three cents higher at A$1.98 after announcing a 29 percent higher full year net profit of A$22.07 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade boomed as the day's 43 point range gave traders plenty of room to work with. Options trade was slow.
Total options traded 26,991
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 10,095
In other local markets, the Australian dollar cooled a little Wednesday as its recent blazing rally drew profit-taking.

The currency stepped back almost 1/2 cent from Tuesday's two-month US$0.7912 high and analysts cautioned it was still overbought on technical indicators so a lapse to US$0.7845 would be no surprise. Nevertheless, sentiment was reportedly bullish and most expected a renewed rise as long as US$0.7820 held.
By 5.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7870/75 after dipping as far as US$0.7872 offshore from a late US$0.7905/10 here on Tuesday.

A late squeeze saw Australian bond yields close around the day's lows, but overall domestic institutions were seen going into U.S. Humphrey-Hawkins testimony short. Local Q4 GDP data proved to be a non-event with little impact. By 5.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), 1o yeat=r T-bonds were yielding 7.82 percent.
